chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Voicing Blues I Like To Hear
summary: Smith explains writing brass and reeds together, the key choice to give altos a weird sound and keep Basie from running all over the piano.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What was your technique? For instance, you'd play the brass off against the reeds or the other way around.
Did you write any stuff where you had the brass and the reeds playing....

Yes. (?).... heard an a little arrangement [INAUDIBLE SECTIONS] ...a thing called "Blues I Like To Hear." At least the last time I talked to him here, he said that's the greatest blues he ever had in his band. "Blues I Like To Hear." I put it in D-natural...
So the trumpets would have been playing in E.

And I put it in (?) to give the altos the weird sound. They had them playing in B. And I put it... The other point was to put it in the key to keep Basie from running all over the piano. All he had to do was to stay right there and comp, and try to stay with the band. And I had all the reeds and the trumpets all playing together.
